question: What is the primary goal of sterilization in a hospital setting?

options.A: Reduction of visible dirt on instruments
options.B: Removal of dangerous chemical toxins only
options.C: Complete elimination of all microbial life
options.D: Prevention of normal flora skin colonization

explanation: Sterilization achieves total destruction of every microorganism, including hardy bacterial spores, unlike methods that only reduce pathogen numbers. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is sterilization critical before performing an invasive clinical procedure?

options.A: It stops patients from developing allergic reactions to metal tools.
options.B: It removes all oily residues left behind by previous manufacturing steps.
options.C: It prevents introducing harmful pathogens directly into sterile body tissues.
options.D: It ensures that medical equipment works at peak mechanical efficiency.

explanation: Invasive procedures break natural body barriers, so any equipment entering sterile tissues must be completely free of microbes to avoid infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which reprocessing step must always happen before disinfection and sterilization?
explanation: Organic soil protects microbes from destruction, meaning dirt must be physically washed away before disinfection or sterilization can work. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is the main difference between disinfection and sterilization?

options.A: Disinfection destroys bacterial spores while sterilization only targets fungi.
options.B: Disinfection is performed on living skin, while sterilization is reserved for air.
options.C: Sterilization eliminates all microbial life including spores, whereas disinfection does not.
options.D: Sterilization uses plain water and soap, whereas disinfection requires heat.

explanation: The defining boundary of sterilization is the complete destruction of resistant bacterial spores, which standard disinfection leaves behind. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which medical device category requires full sterilization according to Spaulding?
explanation: Critical items enter sterile body cavities or the bloodstream, carrying the highest infection risk and demanding complete sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h3)

question: A nurse prepares a gastrointestinal endoscope for a patient. Which Spaulding category does this item fit into?
explanation: Endoscopes contact mucous membranes without penetrating sterile tissues, classifying them as semi-critical devices requiring high-level disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the standard operating pressure and temperature inside a typical steam autoclave?
explanation: Standard autoclave cycles achieve steam sterilization at 121 degrees Celsius under 15 psi of pressure for effective spore destruction. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h4)

question: When would a nurse select dry heat sterilization instead of an autoclave?

options.A: When running a quick emergency cycle for forceps
options.B: When treating anhydrous powders and sharp metal blades
options.D: When processing delicate rubber surgical tubing

explanation: Dry heat is safe for items ruined by moisture or steam, such as powders, oils, and instruments prone to rusting. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why do items sterilized with ethylene oxide gas require a special aeration period?

options.A: To dry off excess water droplets
options.B: To remove lingering toxic chemical residues
options.D: To cool down the hot metal components

explanation: Ethylene oxide is a toxic gas that absorbs into porous materials and must be completely aired out before safe patient contact. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which equipment characteristic makes chemical sterilization necessary over steam autoclaving?

options.A: It is made of heavy stainless steel.
options.C: It has a large surface area.

explanation: Chemical methods like gas plasma or ethylene oxide protect delicate, heat-sensitive instruments from thermal destruction. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which monitoring method uses resistant bacterial spores to confirm actual microbial killing?
explanation: Biological indicators contain actual hardy spores, providing the ultimate proof that the sterilizer killed living microorganisms. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of chemical indicator tape placed on a wrapped instrument tray?

options.A: To measure the exact pounds per square inch of steam inside
options.B: To provide a permanent barcode for hospital inventory tracking
options.C: To prove the internal pack temperature reached lethal levels
options.D: To show that the package has been exposed to the sterilization process

explanation: Chemical indicator tape changes color to distinguish processed items from unprocessed ones, though it does not guarantee complete sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h6)

question: What principle governs the shelf life of properly stored sterile instrument packs?
explanation: Sterility is maintained until an event compromises the packaging, such as a tear, moisture, or a broken seal, rather than expiring by a fixed calendar date. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h7)

question: How should sterile supply shelves be organized in a clinical ward storage room?

options.A: Using a first-in, first-out stock rotation method
options.B: Placing heavier trays directly on the bottom floor
options.C: Storing damp packages until they dry on the shelf
options.D: Stacking items near open windows for fresh air ventilation

explanation: FIFO ensures older stock is used first, preventing packaging degradation and waste from long-term storage. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h7)
